1967-68Copper PlateANDHRA, EAST GODAVARI DISTRICT, RAMACHANDRAPURAM TALUK, Pinapalli1Plates in the possession of Shri Musunuri Sambasivarama Murti.Reddi chief of Rajahmundry.Allāda VēmaŚaka 1346 (Rasa-abdhi-viśva), Krōdhin, Kärttika, ba. 15, Monday=1424 A.D., November 21, f.d.t. 29.Sanskrit, TeluguRecords the grant of the village Pinapanala by the chief after whom the village was renamed as Allada-Vēmabhūpavaram, to his minister Śrīgiri of Harita-gōtra who is said to have undergone the agni-divya (i.e., fire ordeal) to prove that he and his vargas were not guilty of svami-droha. The genealogies of the chief and of Srigiri are given. Published in Bharati, February 1967, pp. 19 ff., and Plates.p30
1967-68Copper PlateASSAM, DARRANG DISTRICT, Dekarchuk (P.O. Jamuguri)2Copper plate in the possession of Shri Mahendra Bhattacharjee, received through Shri J. N. Phukan, Gauhati University, Gauhati.AhomChao-pha Shā-tān (Svargadev Siva-simha).Lāk-ni (i.e. Ahom-era) Kātśau=1714-15 A.D.AhomStates that Chao-pha Shü khung (i.e., Svargadev Rudra-simha), the father of the king, granted in Lak-ni Tao-chau (1697-98) 2 gōts of men or paiks to one brāhmaņa Bagish Bhattacharyya of Kaliabar (Ahom: Tung-rung-dām), on the occasion of the dedication of nam khūm Lung (i.e., the Big Tank) at Chemun (i.e., Rangpur), and (owing probably to the fact that the grant somehow went into desuetude) on being informed by Bhattacharyya's son Raghu (or Raghunandan), the king, in honour of his father's words, granted 2 göts of men (names given) to Raghunandan. Mentions the two tribes, Barua of the Bar Chumchi-ring family and Kataki of the Bar Bailong family. (Remarks given by Shri Phukan).p30

Refers to Jayakēsi of the Manalera family as the feudatory of the king, [Bya]kabbarasi as the wife of the former and Mahāsāmanta Indrakēsi as their son. Registers a grant of land and 30 gadyānas to 12 brāhmaņas of the village for maintaining a satra (chhatra) after laving the feet of 42 mahajanas of the village by Madhukarasa, subordinate of Indrakēsi while the latter was governing Siggāve. Mentions Mailarasa-dandanāyaka probably as the administrator of Bhandivada-grama (Noticed in ASR., 1936-37, p. 98 and SII., Vol. XX, p. xix).p62

1967-68Stone and Other MaterialsAURANGABAD DISTRICT330Same slabChalukya of KalyāņaTribhuvanamallaSaka 1067, Krōśana (Krōdhan a) Pushya śu. 1, Sunday, Uttar-āyana-sańkrānti. Irregular.KannadaRecordsa gift of wet-land, a house and an oil-mill for worship and offerings and for the maintenance of a perpetual lamp to god Uttarēśvara by Dēkiyakka, grand-daughter of Rājimayya after performing the pūḍapuja of her lord Jayakēsi dandanāyaka alias Jayadevayya who was administering Tammiyūru and 12 villages as a subordinate of Kadamba Gūhḷadēva. Among the number of other donors who endowed 5 gadyāna each for maintaining a perpetual lamp in their respective names, may be mentioned Rēvakabbe, the dāyi of Dēkiyakka and Chattikabbe, the kiriyabbe of Jayadevayya.p66
1967-68Stone and Other MaterialsAURANGABAD DISTRICT331Same slab........Saka 1067, Krōśana (Krōdhan a) Pushya śu. 1, Sunday, Uttar-āyana-sańkrānti. Irregular.KannadaStates that when Chattayya was governing the kingdom Ketapayya, the heggade of Māvale-nādu, after offering pādapājā to to Hittimayya, the chief of Tammiyūru and laving the feet of Lākuļēśvara-pandita, endowed 12 houses and 27 mattar of wet-land for the maintenance of the dancing girls of the temple of Uttarēśvara. The donor is said to have paid as kāņika two gadyāņa to the Drodeyas in order to have the endowments made free of all taxes. Mentions Parama-kavi Kannapayya as the composer of the grant and Udayanņa as the engraver. In characters of the 11th century.p66

1967-68Pre-1945-46 CollectionBHILWARA DISTRICT MANDALGARH TAHSIL · Achalgadh2661Stone slab built into the wall of a matha adjoining the temple of Achalēśvara.Guhila of MēdapāṭaSamarasimhaVikrama 1342, Mārgaśīrsha śu. [1].Sanskrit, NāgariGives the genealogy of the Guhila dynasty from Bappa down to the ruler, and records that the ruler caused the renovation of the matha on Mount Arbuda, and arranged for the (daily) feeding of four sages there and erected a golden Achalēśa-daṇḍa at the instance of the Naiṣṭhika Bhāva-śamkara, the disciple of Bhāvāgni, who is stated to have been the head of the matha (sthānādhīśa) in earlier times. The record was composed by Vēdaśarman, son of Priyapatu, written by Subhachandra and engraved by Sūtradhara Karmasimha. Cf. Ind. Ant., Vol. XVI, pp. 345 ff.; Bhandarkar's List, No. 610.p78
1967-68Pre-1945-46 CollectionBHILWARA DISTRICT MANDALGARH TAHSIL · Kankhala (near Achalgadh)2662Stone slab in the Kankhalēśvar mandir.ChaulukyaBhīmadēva (II)Vikrama 1265, Vaiśākha śu. 15, Tuesday = 1209 A. D., April 21.Sanskrit, NāgariRecords that the Saiva pontiff named Kēdārarāśi of the Chapāla sect renovated the temples of Kōtēśvara and Atulanātha, paved the whole of Kanakhala with large stone slabs, erected probably a highwalled enclosure (around the temples), built two temples of Śūlapāṇi and embellished the temple of Kanakhalā-śambhu by erecting in its mandapa a row of pillars. Also records that his sister Sāntā, described as a brahmacharya-parāyaṇā, built a Śiva temple there. Gives the names of the spiritual ancestors of Kēdārarāśi and mentions the king's feudatory Dhārāvarsha ruling at Chandrāvati with Kumāraguru Pralhadana as the Yuvaraja. The record was composed by Lakshmidhara and (engraved) by the Sūtradhara Palhaṇa. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. XI, pp. 220 ff.; Bhandarkar's List, No. 454.p78

1967-68Arabic and PersianBHILWARA DISTRICT MANDALGARH TAHSIL224Top of the same grave(1) A.H. 905 (and words)=A.D. 1499-1500, (2) A.H. 947, Rajab 22-A.D. November 22. 1540, (3) Yuzat II, A.H. 1238, Jumādā II, 11-A.D. February 23. 1823.Persian, Nasta'liq (with few phrases in Naskh.)States that Mirzā Haidar Gorkan, son of Mirza Muhammad Husain Gorkān, and a grandson on daughter's side of Yūnus Khan, and a son of the sister of emperor Bābūr's mother and brother-in-law of Sultan Abū Sa'id Khan, king of Yärkand (in) Maghulistan (Mongolia), son of Sultan Ahmad Khan, son of Yūnus Khan above-mentioned, was a descendant of Tughluq Timür Khan of the time of Chagghtai, son of Changiz Khan and was born on the first date at Uratappa; that in a particular year (not specified) he set out from Yarkand at the orders of Abū Sa'id Khan and conquered (lesser?) Tibet, and in the same (unspecified) year, on Saturday 4th Sha'ban, along with 4,000 horsemen, he conquered Kashmir but handed it over back to its king Muhammad Shah and returned to join his king then oncamped in Tibet; that he was subsequently appointed to L(h)āsa by the king who himself returned to Yarkand but died before reaching there, resulting in uncertainty in the kingdom, whereupon Mirzā Haidar went to Badakhshan and thence to India to emperor Humāyün; that on finding at Lahore that the latter was fleeing to Iran in exile, he went to Kashmir with 450 horsemen, conquered it on the second date and ruled there for the next 10 years till he was killed by one of the members of the public. It further states that Mirzā Haidar was a widely travelled man, having visited the countries of Türān, Maghulistan, and India and had met great men, was a man of erudition and letters and had compiled the Tarikh-i-Rashidi. It further records that this slab was set up at the instance of William Moorcroft Sahib Bahadur, the chief of the British Cavalry (mir akhur-bashi-i-dault-i-Inglisiya), by Sayyid 'Izzatullah Khan, on the third date. Cf. JASB., Vol. XXIII (1864), p. 283; G.M.D. Şüfi, Kashir, Vol. I (Lahore, 1949), pp. 208-09, pl.p100

1971-72Copper Plate1HYDERABAD DISTRICT Hyderabad.—Impression and photo-print of copper-plates in the possession of the Director of Archaeology and Museums, Hyderabad. Through Dr. G. S. Gai. Findspot: Kukkanūru (sic), Bhadrāchalam Taluk, Khammam District, Andhra Pradesh.Chālukya of MudugondaKusumāyudhaTeluguIncomplete. Records that the chief granted the royal insignia and the city Krivvaka in Viṣṇu-nūḍu as an agrahāra on the occasion of śrīkaraṇamu Indapariju and his brother Rāmanāyu, sons of Āyitana-nāyu, belonging to the Kamma-kula, for their loyalty, after their hereditary wealth (kuladhanamutu), their own territory viz., Viṣṇu-nūḍu and all their belongings and had also suffered for 12 years along with those of the king in the battle of Mudugonda. This is dated in the first regnal year of the chief. It is also stated that Kuriyagonneḍu, the lord of Koravipura restored Kusumāyudha. The genealogy of the king is given. In characters of about the 11th century.p38
1971-72Copper Plate2GUJARAT AHMEDABAD DISTRICT Ahmedabad.—Copper-plates in the possession of the Director of Archaeology, Gujarat. Findspot: Ānand, Māngrol Tahsil, Surat District.RāshṭrakūṭaAmōghavarsha IŚaka 772, Āśvayuja śu. 12, Viṣhṇu-saṅkrāntiSanskrit, Early NāgarīIssued from Mānyakhēṭa. Gives the genealogy of the king and records the grant of the village Ānanda situated in the Lāṭa-dēśa, belonging to Bhaṭṭa Lāḍaiya, son of Bhaṭṭa Nāgadēva, who hailed from Pauṇḍrapura-sthāna and was well-versed in the four Vēdas and belonged to the Hārīta-gōtra and was also a student of the Vājasanēya-śākhā. The dūtaka of the record was Nāyēraka-purōhita and the writer was Mahāsāndhivigrahika Haragaṇpa, son of Nāṇṇa. Published in the Journal of Oriental Institute, Baroda, Vol. XX, No. 2, pp. 165 ff.p38

1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsMadhira5Stone pillar lying in a field outside the village.........Śaka 1112 (dina- Vaiśākha śu. 11 (rudra) Wednesday = 1190 A.D., April 18. (The cyclic year was Sādhāraṇa).Sanskrit, TeluguRecords that Nṛisiṁha of Madhunikāpurī situated in Nāṭāḍi (Nāṭavāḍi) and Nāgāṁbā of Divya-vaṁśa and grandson of Narasiṁha and Nāgāṁbā, consecrated (the images of) Sambhu and Viṣṇu and appointed Sāntadēva, a Śiva-vipra, for their worship and for the protection of the temple. It is also stated to have made endowment of 2 khaṇḍikas of land to the deities and 2 drōṇas of land probably to Sāntadēva. Cf. Hyd. Arch. 1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsMāgūru10Stone pillar set up by the side of the Sītārāmasvāmī temple.............TeluguDamaged at the beginning. Records the construction of the Trikuṭa temples of Kēśavadēva, Sūryadēva and probably of Mallikārjuna-mahādēva. Also records the endowment of (one) maṭha on north side of the village and the trees and the other containing 100 kuntas of land. On the east and south of the temples respectively for worship and food-offerings (havi-bali-archana) of the deities and the village-officers on the north of the village and the quarters for the mahājanas to the east of the temple. Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāya Nummadi Duggarāju is stated to have endowed 3 acres of wet-land behind the tank and 3 puttis of land on the western bank of the tank-bank for the worship and food-offerings of Kallikārjuna-mahādēva of the Trikuṭa temples. Do.p44

1971-72Stone and Other Materials82No. 3........Vikrama 1529, Vaiśākha śu. 7, Wednesday = 1472 A.D., April 15.Sanskrit, NāgarīRecords the perpetual obeisance of Sāṁ Hōrīa and Sāṁ Vijaī, the sons of Sāṁ Rāmadēva and his wife Jāsuvī when the Bhaṭṭāraka was śrī Siṁhakīrtidēva of Kunda-kundāchārya āmnāya, Sarasvatī gachchha, Balākāra gaṇa and Mūla saṅgha. The figure of a hamsa (swan) which is the lāñchhana of Sumatinātha is also engraved here.p52
1971-72Stone and Other Materials83No. 4........Vikrama 1529, Vaiśākha śu. 7, Wednesday = 1472 A.D., April 15.Sanskrit, NāgarīRecords the perpetual obeisance of Sāṁ Hōrīa and Sāṁ Vīrabhāna, the sons of Sāṁ Amamsī and his two wives Mādhasī and Madhasī. Amarasi was one of the three sons of Sāṁ Rāmadēva and his wife Jāsuvī, the other two being of Paurapāṭa āmnāya. Mentions Bhaṭṭāraka Siṁhakīrtidēva, the disciple of Bhaṭṭāraka Jinakīrtidēva of Kunda-kundāchārya āmnāya, Sarasvatī gachchha, Balākāra gaṇa and Mūla saṅgha. 1971-72Stone and Other Materials85No. 6........Vikrama 1529, Vaiśākha śu. 7, Wednesday = 1472 A.D., April 15.Sanskrit, NāgarīDo. The figures of two jars, the lāñchhana for Mallinātha are found here.p52

1971-72Stone and Other Materials88No. 9........Vikrama 1529, Vaiśākha śu. 7, Wednesday = 1472 A.D., April 15.Sanskrit, NāgarīIn addition to the contents as given in No. 83 above, supplies some information about the forefathers of Sāṁ Rāmadēva and also states that Sāṁ Vīrabhānu maṁsī had his wife Jāsuvī and (his) sons Sāṁ Jīdhū and Sāṁ Nainasī. 1971-72Stone and Other Materials112Chhatri containing footprints, on the roadside near Dharmagira-kī-Talaiyā.......(1) Vikrama 1823, Māgha ba 5. (2) Vikrama 1837 (3) Vikrama [1911], Pausha śu 13.Local dialect, NāgarīIn three portions. The first portion, in the front, records the death of Muto Bāsha(kha) tamalaji, the son of Muto Chunnamaji mahājana (i.e. a merchant) on the first date and the construction of the chhatri on the date. The second portion, to the right of the footprint, records the renovation probably of the chhatri, on the third date by Lālābhūdana. The third portion on the other one, some of which belonged to Gwalior State, gives details of the size of the footprints, records that the chhatri was constructed on the bank of the tank on the field belonging to Gusainī Rājachandra and Dīvānajī by Rūpachandra. Dīvānajī chandra when Ousahi Rājyams was the pontiff. The masons were Bālākisana and Gamgārāma. For the first portion Cf. ibid., No. 512.p55

1971-72Stone and Other Materials114TIKAMGARH DISTRICT TIKAMGARH TAHSIL Ahār.—Pedestal of the main image in the Jain temple in the Digambar Jain-k’hētra.ChandēllaParamardidēva (Paramardin)Vikrama 1237, Mārgaśīrsha śu 3, Friday=1180 A.D., November 21.Sanskrit, NāgarīRecords the construction of the chaitya of Śānti (Śāntinātha) by the brothers Jāhaḍa and Udayachandra [*], who were the sons of the merchant Dēdhaka, the son of Rālhā and Rālhā was who built a Śānti-chaityālaya in the village of Ahāra and another at Madanāuse(śa)śāṁganampur. 1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsMAHARASHTRA KOLHAPUR DISTRICT HATEKANANGALE TALUK Hāḍe134Slab set up in the Pārśvanātha basadi.ŚilāhāraMahāmaṇḍalēśvara ruling from Valavāḍa.Śaka 1040, Viļambi, Āshāḍha śu. 5, Wednesday, June 5, 1118 A.D.KannadaRegisters the grant of 12 mattar of land to the basadi built by the chief of the village situated in Eḍe-nāḍu, by the king at the instance of Nāgaladēvī on the occasion of the lunar eclipse. 1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsRāmāpur135Slab leaning against the wall of Pārśvanātha basadi.ŚilāhāraMahāmaṇḍalēśvaraŚaka 1073, Pramādi, Bhādrapada Paurṇamī, Friday, lunar eclipse, 1150 A.D., September 8.Sanskrit, KannadaGives the genealogy of the chief and registers the grant of land measuring 4 nivartanas measured by Kīmḍidēśa-daṇḍa, a garden at the village of Rāmāpura, to the basadi at the same place as the village of Maḍalūra for the worship (ashṭa-vidhārcchana) and for the repairs and renovation of the Pārśvanātha temple which was built by Chaudhare Kāma-dēva. The gift was entrusted to the āchārya of the basadi, Siddhāntadēva, the disciple of Māghanandi-siddhāntadēva-dēva-tho āchārya of the Rūpanārāyaṇa-chaityālaya at Kshulla-kapura (Kolhāpura). 1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsTorapaḷḷi207Rock called ‘Ruḍrapāda-gaḷabhaṇḍa’ in the village.Mysore chiefsChikka-Dēvarāja-voḍeya, ruling from Śrirangapaṭṭaṇa.Śaka 1590, Raktākshi, Pushya ba. 1.TamilRecords the construction of a dam named as Nañjarāja-sāgara across the river Ponnaiyāru, a tributary of the Bhadra-giri Trikūṭēśvarasvāmi on the banks of the river, Piṇākini by Nañjarājayya of Daḷavāyikshatriya-vaṃśa, and Bhāradvāja-gōtra, the younger brother of Koṇḍarāja and other sons of the chief of the Mysore family, Hosavūr. The construction was done with the blessings of his (Nañjarājayya’s) family preceptor, Svāmikēśvara Padmā-rasa-dēva and at the instance of his elder brother, the king, as an act of devotion to gods Mallikārjunadēva of Arala and Nañjuṇḍēśvara of Nañjuṇḍuḍu for the benefit and welfare of his family members viz., his father Nañjarājayya, his mother Liṅgāmbā-dēvamma and his younger brother Vīrarā-jayya and his own sons.p69

1971-72Stone and Other MaterialsVARANASI DISTRICT · Tokyo307Photographs of an inscription on the image of a Buddha, i.e. Mahāvairocana received from Professor Takayasu Higuchi, Faculty of letters, Kyoto University, Japan, through Shri B. K. Thapar, Director General of Archaeology, New Delhi. Findspot: Kandahār, Afghanistan.Sanskrit, BrāhmīLate Contains a verse in anuṣṭubh metre in praise of Śiva describing him as the very embodiment of the three mūrttis i.e. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva as the creator, protector and destroyer. Refer to another verse in anuṣṭubh stated to have been told by Lord Mahādēva himself as corroborating his three fold aspect. In characters of about the 8th century A.D. Published in Studies in Indian Epigraphy (Jnl. of the Ep. Soc. of India), vol. I pp. 1 ff. and plate.p79

Records that Sam° Dharaṇaka, the son of Kāmalade and Sam° Kumapāla and the grandson of Sam° Māṅgaṇa of Prāg-vāṭa family, belonging to the line of Sāḍā, Jāvada and others born of his wife Dhāraladevi, well as his elder brother Sam° Rātṇā and his wife Rākhā and their sons Lākhā, Mājā, Sōmā and Sāligā caused to be constructed at Rāṇapura a temple of Chaumukha (Chaturmukha) of Rīshabha, called Trailōkyadīpaka. The temple was consecrated by Sōmasundara-sūri of Bṛhadgaccha and Jayachandrasūri of Bṛhadgaccha-sūri-sūtradhāra. The construction was made by sūtradhāra Dēpāka, a Trāvaḍa. Cf. A.R. 1992-93Stone and Other MaterialsNORTH ARCOT AMBEDKAR DISTRICT425Central shrine, Tirumeraliśvara temple.'Do.Rājarāja I....TamilAmrēśvaram-udaiyar every month on the day of sādaiyam the natal star of Rājarāja I and also for large scale food offerings on the occasion of festivals on the day of Aviţţam, the birth star of Kundavai, the elder sister of Rājarāja every month. It is stated that this arrangement was to be carried out with surplus paddy that was deducted after due enquiry by the revenue administrator of the district.p80

1992-93Stone and Other MaterialsNORTH ARCOT AMBEDKAR DISTRICT427On the east wall, Central shrine, Tirumeraliśvara temple.ChōļaRājakēsari....TamilRecords the gift of a quarter veli of land in two pieces by Alangudaiyān Malapādi Kumaran, the accountant of Tiruvāmaniśvarattu Mahādēva temple at Pāchchil in Malanādu. The produce of the land 22 kalam, one tuni and one padakku obtained after the reclamation of land is to be utilised for supplying one ulakku of oil daily to burn the lamp to the deity of the above temple. The donor also donated one lamp-stand to burn the lamp. Do. Damaged. Records a gift of sixteen kalañju of gold to burn two lamps during the day times perpetually to the deity of Tirumergaļi at Pachchil by the singer of the temple Samarakēsari Nittappērarāyan.p80
1992-93Stone and Other MaterialsNORTH ARCOT AMBEDKAR DISTRICT428On the south wall, Central shrine, Avanisundarēśvara temple.ChōļaRājarājēndra-chola....TamilRefers to the enquiry conducted by the officials Irumudichōļa Mūvēnda vēļār, Parakēsari Vilupparaiyar and others into the misdemeanour (not-specified) committed by Korrangudi Pannāinallür Udaiyan who held the kani of writing accounts of the temple of Pachchil in Pächchil-kūṟṟam. As the accountant was found guilty, a fine of 100 kāśu was imposed on him. As he was unable to remit the fine it was decided to sell his lands, houses, gardens at Kõrrangudi and Pālainallūr, which were obviously given for writing the accounts by the temple. Since no body came forward to purchase the same, it was decided to sell the same to the temple itself along with the right to maintain temple accounts. The amount thus realised, after the sale, was deposited in the temple treasury. It was also decided to make their own provisions for maintaining temple accounts.p81

1995-96Copper Plate1Tirupati. — A copper-plate charter in possession of Dr. N.Krishna Reddy, Department of Ancient History, Archaeology and Culture, S.V.University, Tirupati. Findspot: Âlavakoṇḍa, Sanjamala mandal (Part of old Koilkuntla Taluk), Kurnool District. Impressions through Dr. C.APadmanabha Sastry, A.S.E., Southern Zone, Chennai.Early PallavasVishnugōpavarmaYear 1, Hēmanta, paksha prathama di. 5Prakrit mixed with Sanskrit, Southern CharactersRecords the gift of the village Khaṇjahappā-kuṇḍūra located in Mimali-raṭṭa in Chirippālikā-rājya to a brāhmaṇa called Sīvaradajja belonging to the Kāśyapa-gōtra as brahmadēya by the king, probably for the longevity of his father Buddhavarma. Certain usual privileges were allowed to the gift village. The gift was made in the presence of bhōjaka and other officials. In characters of the 4th-5th century A.D. Published in Śānkaram (Sankaranarayanan Fel. Vol.), pp. 67 ff. and plates.p30
1995-96Copper Plate2Do. - Photographs supplied by Dr. K. K. Choudhary, Reader in the same department. Findspot: Not known.VijayanagaraKrishṇadēvarāyaŚaka 1435, Śrīmukha, Kārttika, Uthāna-dvādaśīSanskrit, NandināgarīFirst plate missing. Records the grant of the village Mājāmbūka alias Nāgalādēvī-samudra situated in the Kōnāma-nāḍu, in the Changalapaṭṭus[i]mā]. belonging to Āmūru-kōṭa in Toṇḍaimanḍala division of Paduviḍu-rājya to a brāhmaṇa named Ōbhala, son of [Jā]lkuduga, belonging to Vasiṣṭha-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra. The grant was stated to have been made by the king in the presence of god Vīrūpākṣa, on the banks of Tuṅgabhadra river after making the gift village free from encumbrances and taxes.p31
1995-96Copper Plate3Do. - Do.VijayanagaraŚrī Raṅgarāya IIIŚaka 156 . (. ṛitu-bāṇa-chandra)Sanskrit, NandināgarīRecords the tax-free gift of Pālamarigalam alias Śrī Raṅgariyapuram situated in Toṇḍaimandalam of Chaṇḍagiri-rājya to Śrī Veṅkaṭādri, son of Śrī Lakṣmaṇa belonging to Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Viśvāmitra-gōtra.p31

Vēlupu-koṇḍa, Urukoṇḍa, Maddicharuvu and Atukūru in the Tāļupāka-vishaya with all privileges and exemption of all taxes to the ascetics of Āryabhikshu-samgha, who performed dhyāna-adhyayana, etc., and resided at the mahāvihāra at Varddhamāna, which was established by Mahā-Meghavāhana, by the king, issued through mahāmāra for the merit of his grandmother. 1995-96Copper Plate5Do. - Do.VijayanagaraPṛthvī Śrī MūlarājaYear 43, Phālguṇa śu. 3Sanskrit, Southern CharactersRecords the gift of the village called Aṭṭaluvuḍu situated in the midst of the villages Karakuṇḍa, Kamsāryya, Velkuṇḍukuriki, Maṇivardda and Pallaveñcha, in Talupāka-viṣaya to the asceitics of Ārya-bhikṣu-samgha belonging to the 18 sections (nikāya) who had come from four directions and resided at the famous mahāvihāra on the eastern skirts of Guṇapāśapura hill for their clothing, food, beds, seats and medical treatment by the king from his provincial capital Nandivardhana. 1995-96Stone and Other Materials40Do. - On the north bhitti of the same shrine.ChōlaParakēsarinarmanRegnal year 16TamilRecords that an individual Puļuīyūr-uḍaiyān Tiruvīśalūr Sūryan alias Edirmēr-Śikaṇḍappēraraiyan of Puļuīyūr donated 100 kalam of paddy to the god of Tiruvīśalūr alias Śrī Avanīṇārāyanchaturvēdimangalam, a dēvadāna-brahmadēyam to meet the expenditure (of employing persons) for playing the drum etc., at the temple. Muhammad Tahsīn, the royal eunuch (of Shāh ‘Ālam II) enclosed the place as a mark of respect, desiring that this stone (spot) should become a place of pilgrimage. Noticed in List of Muhammadan and Hindu Monuments, Vol. I (Calcutta, 1916), p. 147.p88
1995-96Pre-1945-46 CollectionKARNATAKA MANDYA DISTRICT SRIRANGAPATNA TALUK Śrīraṅgapaṭṇa.2Loose slab kept in the Tipu Sultan Research Institute. Gumbad-i-Śāhī. Originally from Gañjam. (Do.)........(1) A.H. 1213, Ramaḍān 26 = 1799 A.D., March 3 (2) A.H. 1213, Ramaḍān 27 = 1799 A.D., March 4 (3) A.D. 1825 (4) A.D. 1830 (5) A.D. 1835 (6) A.H. 1283, Muḥarram 5 = 1866 A.D., May 20Urdū, Nasta‘līqRecords the martyrdom of Muḥammad Riḍā ‘Alī Khān alias Banki Nawwāb, Chief-Head (Mīr-i-Mīrān) of Zuṃra (Corps to act as Body-Guard of Ṭīpū Sulṭān) in the battle of Kuḍak (ie. Gadaɡ), following a musket-shot, on the first date. Also records that the dead-body dejected by his death, Ṭīpū Sulṭān issued a royal order, saying that the dead-body should be buried at the platform of the Śhāhī Gumbad (ie. in the royal graveyard) in accordance with the religious injunction for a martyr. Thus, according to the order, the deceased was buried on the second date. Further states that the martyr was the son of Nawwāb Ibrāhīm ‘Alī Khān, governor of Bangalore (Ḥākim-i-Banglūr) and a saintlyp89
1995-96Pre-1945-46 Collectiontwo sons Muḥammad Ibrāhīm ‘Alī Khān and Muḥammad Qāsim ‘Alī Khān and three daughters (names not given) were till then alive. April 17 (3) A.H. 1308 (& 18 chronograms) = 1890 A.D. August 17 - 1891 A.D. August 6Persian, Nasta‘līqThis epitaph of great interest, replete with as many as eighteen chronograms of one Shaikh Husain on the third date (A.H.1308). Each chronogram yielding A.H. 1308, is composed in such a way that according to the meaning, various aspects of the career of the deceased Shaikh Husain, come to light. We get various pieces of information about the deceased that he was born on the first date (A.H. 1233) and joined the British army as a soldier on the second date (A.H. 1251) and served with great efforts and merit for forty-four years. Further records that because of his laudable service career, he was honoured with the titles of Sardār Bahādur and Najm-i Hind (i.e. Star of India). He was one of the spiritual successors of Sayyid Banda Nawāz Gesū Darāz. He left Nāgpūr forp117

1995-96Pre-1945-46 Collection131Qabrastān in Shāhzādgān. Tomb of ʿAbbās Khān. Headstone of the grave.1969 A.D., April 15Urdū, NastaʿlīqShājahānpūr. Composed by Abr. Records the history and political career of the family of Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, son of Yāsīn Khān, son of Ismāʿīl Khān, of the Dilāzāk Karrānī tribe (of the Afghāns). Also records that Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, migrated from his native place Mātūrī or Shivgī, District Mardān, to India in the ending years of the reign of Jahāngīr. During the time of migration, he stayed in the village Surāī Ṣāliḥ, a stronghold of the Dilāzāks. Later he made his stay in Jalandhar where his brother Sayyid Muḥammad Khān had settled permanently. Afterwards, he halted for some time at Khūrja and Basai in Bulandshahr District. Ultimately, in the early years of Shājahān’s period, about 1632 A.D. he laid the foundation of Shājahānpūr. After his migration to India, ʿAbbās Khān enrolled himself in the service of Prince Dārā Shikoh. But on 24th Muḥarram A.H. 1059, corresponding to 22nd October 1650 A.D. (irregular - it should be 28th January, 1649 A.D.), hep134
1995-96Pre-1945-46 Collectionleft the service of Dārā Shikoh at Achhrā Lāhore and joined the service of Prince Aurangzeb who bestowed on him the manṣab of One Thousand and Two Hundred swār. After five days, on 29 Muḥarram (A.H. 1059 = 2 February 1649 A.D.), it was raised to One Thousand and Four Hundred and finally to 26th Rabī II, A.H. 1069, corresponding to 22 January 1659 A.D. (irregular - it should be 11 January 1659 A.D.). It further states that ‘Abbās Khān accompanied with his force under the command of Mīr Jumla against Prince Shujā‘, brother of Aurangzeb. On 5th April 1660 A.D., corresponding to 4 Jumādā II, A.H. 1071 (irregular - it should be 4 Sha‘bān, A.H. 1070) at the time of the sun-rising when the large armies entered a narrow ghāṭ near the city Mālda four miles below the Baglā Ghāṭ (present Bholāhaṭ) of thep135
